papers.title: DiscoDemo: Discovering Efficient and Diverse Robot Demonstrations for Imitation Learning
papers.problem: Robot learning from demonstrations fails when the demonstrations cover only one narrow way to do the task.
papers.fix: The authors used a reinforcement learning generator to make varied successful demonstrations, lifting real-robot success from 39% to 78%.
papers.practicalUseCase: Varied demonstrations beat repeated ones, so collect different ways to finish a task before you collect more of the same.
papers.limitation: The result covers four manipulation tasks and one pretrained robot model family.

papers.title: Function-Space Temporal Self-Distillation for Policy Optimization
papers.problem: Training language models to reason with only pass-or-fail scores gives weak feedback, and self-teaching setups drift unstably.
papers.fix: FSPO beat the best baseline by about 4 points and cut peak memory from 70 GB to 56 GB.
papers.practicalUseCase: You can train a stronger reasoning model on less memory, so cheaper hardware may be enough for fine-tuning.
papers.limitation: The tests used one model family, Olmo3-7B-Instruct, under a 5-hour training budget.

papers.title: How Much Feedback Is Needed to Break Template Protection? The Geometric Vulnerability of Biometric Authentication
papers.problem: Biometric systems that reveal only accept or reject were thought to protect stored face templates from rebuilding.
papers.fix: Attackers rebuilt protected templates from accept or reject answers alone, and a face prior cut the queries needed 5 times.
papers.practicalUseCase: A hidden template is not safe if the login check leaks answers, so limit and monitor repeated failed attempts.
papers.limitation: The work shows the attack method, and it does not measure how well real deployed systems resist it.

papers.title: Kolab: Benchmarking Human-Agent Collaboration in Long-Horizon Workflows
papers.problem: Agent benchmarks test whether AI finishes a task alone, not whether experts accept its work during long projects.
papers.fix: Top AI models overestimated how well experts collaborate with them and could not tell good collaboration from bad.
papers.practicalUseCase: Do not trust an AI agent's own claim that the teamwork went well, so check its output yourself.
papers.limitation: The dataset has 50 professionals and over 115 hours of recordings, which is small.

papers.title: WORTH Benchmark: Evidence Discovery under Not-Fully-Cooperative Information -- A Two-Episode Pilot
papers.problem: Reasoning tests give models the clues up front, so they never test how models find evidence on their own.
papers.fix: In 31 of 37 runs, models named the same wrong suspects, picking suspicion clues 25 times and exoneration clues never.
papers.practicalUseCase: Models can pick clues that support a wrong answer, so ask an AI for evidence against its own conclusion.
papers.limitation: This pilot covers two episodes only and does not rank models or show a general cause.

papers.title: Sharīʿah Compliance in Malaysia’s Digital Payment Systems: Evidence from Expert Interviews
papers.venue: International Journal of Islamic Finance and Sustainable Development
papers.leadAuthor: Wan Anis Wan Mohd Assrudin et al.
papers.problem: Malaysian digital payment services face doubts about real Shariah compliance, mostly among providers that are not banks.
papers.fix: Ten Shariah experts said non-bank payment providers have weaker governance, and also raised data risks and low consumer awareness.
papers.practicalUseCase: Check who governs a payment app's Shariah rules before you trust the label, since non-bank apps have less oversight.
papers.limitation: The study covers Malaysia only and rests on interviews with ten experts.

papers.title: Interest Prohibitions and Contract Design in Medieval Christianity and Islam
papers.venue: International Journal of Islamic Finance and Sustainable Development
papers.problem: Medieval lenders in Europe and Islamic lands both faced interest bans, and how each side coped was unclear.
papers.fix: European lenders hid return inside indirect contracts, while Islamic traditions put return in trade and partnerships with shared risk.
papers.practicalUseCase: A contract's label matters less than who owns the asset and who carries the loss, so check those first.
papers.limitation: The paper reviews doctrine and secondary history, with no new archives and no prevalence figures.

papers.title: Financial Depth and Stability in Dual Banking Systems
papers.venue: International Journal of Islamic Finance and Sustainable Development
papers.problem: Evidence was thin on whether adding Islamic banking beside conventional banks helps a country's economy grow.
papers.fix: Across 27 countries over 2010 to 2024, more Islamic finance raised private credit (0.3725) and yearly real output (0.0842).
papers.practicalUseCase: Islamic banking looks like a growth partner to conventional banks, so policymakers can back it without replacing existing banks.
papers.limitation: The study compares only dual-banking countries, so it cannot show how they differ from single-system countries.

papers.title: Financing Government Issuances via Service Ownership Ṣukūk
papers.venue: International Journal of Islamic Finance and Sustainable Development
papers.problem: Gulf governments with budget deficits and high unemployment lack a Shariah-compliant way to borrow against public jobs.
papers.fix: A Gulf simulation showed the new sukuk cut deficits by 1.5 GDP points and borrowing costs by 62 basis points.
papers.practicalUseCase: If the model holds, governments could fund jobs and cut deficits together, but the idea needs legal and market testing.
papers.limitation: The model treats households as identical and may not fit lower-income Muslim-majority countries.

papers.title: Global prevalence of impostor phenomenon in medical students: A systematic review and meta-analysis
papers.institution: National University Toribio Rodríguez de Mendoza
papers.problem: Medical students may feel like frauds despite their success, and nobody had pooled the worldwide figures.
papers.fix: Impostor feelings were common among medical students worldwide, though results varied a lot by sampling method and region.
papers.practicalUseCase: If you feel like a fraud, you are far from alone, so talk to peers before it hurts your work.
papers.limitation: The pooled numbers vary widely between studies, so treat any single prevalence figure with caution.

papers.title: Exploring the influencing factors of academic doctoral students’ academic innovation behavior in the context of generative artificial intelligence: Self-determination theory and motivation-opportunity-ability perspectives
papers.problem: Doctoral students use generative AI very differently, and it was unclear what drives their new ideas.
papers.fix: Both inner drive and outside rewards raised doctoral students' innovative work, and long unmet psychological needs sharply cut it.
papers.practicalUseCase: Protect your motivation and basic needs first, because AI tools will not rescue a burnt-out researcher.
papers.limitation: The data are one-time self-reports from chemistry students, so they cannot prove cause.
